plan.competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the meaning, importance, and sources of history
plan.general_objectives: Explain the concept of History, the qualities and dating of historical events, its importance, relationships with other subjects, and sources of historical information.
plan.specific_objectives: By the end of the lesson the student should be able to: Explain the meaning of History and its basic concepts; identify the qualities that make an event historical; explain the ways of dating historical events (time units, BC/AD/BCE/CE, timelines); explain the importance of studying History; relate History to Geography, Civics, and Economics; describe primary and secondary sources of historical information.
plan.teaching_aids: History textbook, concept charts, timeline wall charts, source samples, flashcards
plan.remarks: The students who did not understand the lesson well will be in the remedial class. Otherwise I will proceed with the topic.

plan.competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of the origin of human beings and early technology
plan.general_objectives: Explain the theories of human origin, the major groups of human ancestors, and the development of early human technology.
plan.specific_objectives: By the end of the lesson the student should be able to: Describe the Creation Theory and the Theory of Evolution (Charles Darwin); describe early human ancestors (Australopithecus, Homo habilis); describe advanced human ancestors (Homo erectus, Homo sapiens); examine early human technology (Old, Middle, Late Stone Age and Iron Age).
plan.sub_topic: Theories of the origin of human beings
plan.teaching_aids: Evolution tree chart, hominid diagrams, Olduvai Gorge illustrations, stone tool model kits

plan.general_objectives: Explain the concepts of social organisation and economic production, and the pre-colonial modes of production in Africa.
plan.specific_objectives: By the end of the lesson the student should be able to: Define production, instruments of labour, and subjects of labour; explain social organization and social relations of production; describe the Communal, Slavery, and Feudalism modes of production and their African forms (Unyarubanja, Umwinyi).

plan.sub_topic: Concepts of social organisation and economic production
plan.teaching_aids: Production elements chart, socio-economic structure diagram, feudal hierarchy diagram, East Africa map

plan.competence: 4.0 Demonstrate mastery of agricultural development in pre-colonial Africa
plan.general_objectives: Explain agriculture and the transition from hunting and gathering to farming, and the types of agricultural practices in pre-colonial Africa.
plan.specific_objectives: By the end of the lesson the student should be able to: Define agriculture and explain the Neolithic Revolution; describe shifting cultivation and bush fallowing; describe permanent crop cultivation and pastoralism; examine advanced agricultural techniques (terracing and irrigation).

plan.teaching_aids: Transition infographic chart, shifting cultivation diagrams, regional agricultural map, terracing and irrigation diagrams

plan.competence: 6.0 Demonstrate mastery of social, political, and education systems in pre-colonial Africa
plan.general_objectives: Explain the concepts of social, political, and education systems, the non-centralised political systems, and the education system in pre-colonial African societies.
plan.specific_objectives: By the end of the lesson the student should be able to: Explain the concepts of social, political, and education systems; describe non-centralised political systems (clan-based organization, age-set system); describe the indigenous education system (informal learning, initiation ceremonies).
plan.main_topic: SOCIAL, POLITICAL AND EDUCATION SYSTEMS IN PRE-COLONIAL AFRICA
plan.sub_topic: Concepts of social, political and education systems
plan.teaching_aids: System structure chart, clan tree diagram, age-set hierarchy chart, informal learning methods chart

plan.competence: 7.0 Demonstrate mastery of state organisation in pre-colonial Africa
plan.general_objectives: Explain the meaning of a state and describe the centralised states and kingdoms of pre-colonial Africa.
plan.specific_objectives: By the end of the lesson the student should be able to: Describe the meaning of a state and factors for state formation; describe centralised states in East Africa (Buganda, Bunyoro, Karagwe); describe Western Sudanic states (Ghana, Mali, Songhai) and Forest states of West Africa (Oyo, Dahomey, Asante); describe Central African kingdoms (Kongo, Luba, Lunda) and Southern African kingdoms (Mwenemutapa, Great Zimbabwe, Zulu).
plan.teaching_aids: Maps of pre-colonial African states and kingdoms, state formation concept chart, regional summary wall chart
